title: openai-compat: tool schema mapping, tool_choice semantics, and tool message formatting
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: our OpenAI compatibility layer's previous approach to tool/function calling left gaps around schema mapping and the semantics of tool_choice which caused inconsistent behavior across hosted and private deployments. This PR centralizes tool schema mapping, formalizes tool_choice semantics to match OpenAI's intent (explicit selection vs suggested tools), and normalizes the formatting of tool messages emitted into assistant/tool streams. Summary of changes: 1) introduce a deterministic mapper that converts Redwood tool descriptors to OpenAI-style schemas including required/optional properties, canonical type coercions, and enum normalization; 2) implement tool_choice handling for three modes (explicit, suggested, and prefer_local) so runtime routing and the compatibility layer agree on whether a model decision is authoritative; 3) change assistant->tool message formatting to produce a stable, compact JSON payload and ensure streaming chunk boundaries are tool-agnostic; 4) add end-to-end tests that validate mapping fidelity against representative tool manifests and simulated model choices; 5) update docs and examples to show expected tool_choice behaviors and the recommended schema annotations. Testing & CI: unit tests added for mapper and tool_choice logic; integration test exercising streaming and tool handoff against the compat shim; a resilience test that replays a previously flaky tool-selection case. Why this approach: keeping mapping deterministic reduces subtle regressions when model or client libraries evolve; explicitly encoding tool_choice modes makes routing policies simpler and safer for Dedicated/Private deployments. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOLCHOICE=v1 for 2 weeks in staged rollout then enable by default if no regressions. See linked Linear tasks ENG-1342 and ENG-1399 for follow-ups and telemetry goals.

review_comments: Diego Marquez (reviewer): Can you clarify how enum coercion handles mixed-type enums? Suggest adding an explicit precedence rule.
Author (Asha): Added a precedence table and unit tests to test_tool_mapper.py that show string->number coercion is disabled by default; numeric enums preserve numeric types.
Linnea Ko (reviewer): The streaming formatter change looks good but we saw a small regression in chunk boundary tests in CI; please add a deterministic chunking mode for tests.
Author (Asha): Added deterministic_chunking=true for test harness and adjusted integration expectations. CI green locally.
Samir Rao (approver): Approve after addressing telemetry hooks and feature flagging for rollout. Left suggestions for minor doc wording which are resolved.
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: improved tool schema mapping, explicit tool_choice semantics, and more stable tool message formatting. Backwards-compatible; feature-flagged during staged rollout. See openai-compat.md for migration notes.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOLCHOICE flag. Rollout to staging then canary for Dedicated clusters. Watch telemetry ENG-1342 for model/tool mismatch rates and routing fallbacks.
manual_steps: Enable feature flag via config map or env var OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOLCHOICE=v1, restart compat service; to rollback set OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOLCHOICE=off and restart.
documentation_updates: Updated openai-compat.md and openai-compat-tool-choice.md with examples showing explicit vs suggested tool_choice flows and example mappings for common schema patterns.
testing_notes: Added deterministic chunking option for streaming tests and added fixture manifests that cover nested objects, optional/required fields, and enum edge cases. Integration tests validate end-to-end handoff including tool selection telemetry events.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: behavioral change is feature-flagged and covered by unit+integration tests. Main risk is clients relying on previous lenient coercions; mitigation is docs and telemetry to detect mismatches.
